name: Node API
rationale: Node APIs stay testable when routes own transport mapping, services own business workflows, and adapters own infrastructure.

sources.label: Node API layered architecture
sources.note: Rules encode thin controller and typed configuration conventions common to Express/Fastify/Hono services.

directories.purpose: HTTP route definitions and request/response mapping.
External services, storage, queues, email, and payment adapters.

fileRules.name: Thin controllers
fileRules.rule: Route handlers should validate input, call a service, and map the response. They should not own business workflows.
fileRules.trigger: A route/controller file contains business workflow logic or exceeds the line threshold.
fileRules.recommendation: Move orchestration into src/server/services and keep route files focused on HTTP mapping.
fileRules.goodExample: route.ts parses input and calls createInvoiceService.
fileRules.badExample: route.ts validates input, updates multiple tables, sends email, and computes billing state.

fileRules.name: No direct env spread
fileRules.rule: Environment variables should be parsed once through typed configuration.
fileRules.recommendation: Create a typed config module and import validated settings from there.
fileRules.badExample: const apiKey = process.env.API_KEY in many modules.

moduleBoundaries: Routes depend on services; services depend on repositories/adapters; adapters do not import routes.
Validation schemas should be reusable between route handling and tests.
testingExpectations: Services should be testable without starting an HTTP server.
At least one integration test should cover route validation and response shape.
agentInstructions: Do not implement an API as one large server.ts/app.ts file.
Keep auth, validation, service logic, and infrastructure adapters separate.
